summary: The finite classification and the general family-A lower bound withstand the checks completed here. Exact lower certificates cover every stated pair, and exact chains at all essential chamber vertices supply the matching upper bound. The extra unpadded forms and exact rank-forcing example are reproduced. No unresolved material mathematical objection was found. The six-family all-m description and broader rank rule remain conjectural/numerical.
strengths: Independent new LR cell-tableau code and integer coefficient assembly verifies all 875 certificates (4342 tiles), including every newly completed larger pair.
The 3x3 Horn-chain construction correctly preserves only the common spectrum between steps, and its feasibility region is a polyhedral projection on the fixed ordered stratum.
Exact exposedness witnesses establish irredundancy and strict interior exposure for all 526 z0,z1 forms.
The family-A proof handles the last short layer with either a Lidskii tile or Weyl tiles; independent bookkeeping verified 15582 cases m=3..30,z=0..5.
Strict rational padding margins and the full Horn optimal-face calculation distinguish lower cost from minimal optimal rank.
weaknesses: The main classification is finite (m<=9,z<=2); numerical continuation does not establish the six-family conjecture.
The exact chamber computation relies on pycddlib/GMP vertex enumeration and LP correctness, not a separately verified proof assistant.
The explicit numerical matrix constructor is diagnostic and has documented larger residuals at some degenerate points; it is unnecessary for the exact existence proof.
Broad priority was not certified, and the previously known padding example is illustrative rather than a new counterexample.
